describes: The map registry (decisions §5 D8.1, D5.1, D5.4, D5.10, §15 S3 and S4). Each map's channels, what each stores, owner, unit, texel, format and encoder, readers, what rebuilds it and where it is resident; how pages are charted, which format each takes, and who bakes them. Fields are coarse and owned by the land; place and history maps are fine and owned by the page group, sampled from the fields and the chunks' geometry. Maps store inputs (a drive per texel and layer, the clock's reach, the place's feet and water, the light's inputs); the shell atlas is the one cached output. Lengths in millimetres.

ch.is: the draw chunk: draws, rebuilds and keys the mesh at l0 and l1, and is the pick slot

pg.is: the page group: one set of place and history pages for its 4 x 4 chunks, addressed by uv1, rebaked by region

ce.is: the cell: merges l2 and l3, and holds a shell atlas

lc.is: the land and streaming chunk: fields, height and ground; a container file of near levels

bk.is: the block: merges l4; a container file of its records, shells, l4 and ground

faceClasses.rule: The plan sets each surface region's face class from what the face is (facing) and what it looks onto, by this table and nothing else; tools/validate_record.py checks every region against it. A combination not in the table is an error.
decisions: A face to steps or to the harbour is a street face: steps are walked, and a face to the water is the town's front from the sea and the quay.
A wall's face to earth (a retaining wall's buried back) is ground: it is seen, if ever, as ground.

street.note: the material's texel on every floor

yard.note: the material's texel to 2 m above the ground the face meets, where splash, damp and contact sit; 80 mm above

texel.marks: A mark's texel is half its smallest feature (two texels across it), from the part's marks.
texel.rule: A surface's texel is the coarser (the larger) of its face class's texel and the finest of its parts' mark texels.
texel.status: FIRM as a rule (S3); the waste provisional

shellAtlas.note: baked on demand within l3's reach; a shell draws plain from its material class and reset year until its atlas lands; a block reads cached small mips where they exist and draws plain elsewhere; no atlas ships city-wide

rebake.runs: on the GPU behind the dated card
rebake.status: provisional; drawing a page measured at 0.7 ms, CPU compression 5.3 to 8.7 ms, so compression is on the GPU

charts.per: a run of one face kind (a wall's face, a flight unrolled along its walking line), its joints inside: drives are continuous across joints, and clocks are per piece
charts.fill: barycentric, then dilation over the whole page; the three mips baked within each chart
charts.packing: shelf; MaxRects if the waste passes texel.packingWastePerMille
charts.why: A BC block at mip m covers 4 x 2^m texels of mip 0, so a 16-texel grid keeps three mips block-pure. At 80 m a 2 cm texel reads at about mip 1.5, so three mips suffice. Charts per run waste about 10 to 15 per cent, per piece 25 to 70.
charts.status: FIRM; shimmer at chart borders is judged at step 3's R6 (unknowns: chart-shimmer)

pageFormat.source: RGBA8, linear (sRGB off, alpha not transparency), with the baker's own mips (charts), until a page's own error is measured
pageFormat.rule: Each page's GPU format is chosen from a real page's BC7 error: per channel, mips 0 to 2, the 99th percentile at most 2/255. h1.b's line is about 1/255 stored, since moss scales its error by up to 2.04. A channel pair that fails goes to a BC5 page and costs a sample (D5.10).
pageFormat.when: at the end of step 3's R3, before R4: no real page exists earlier
pageFormat.grain: none in pages: the fine marks come from noise in uv2 (D5.8)
pageFormat.status: FIRM as a rule; each page's format is unknown until R3 (unknowns: page-format)

bakers.rule: One bake function serves the editor and the player, held to golden page hashes beside the kind's stage goldens (fixtures/golden/<kind>/), so what is judged is what ships.
bakers.exception: Step 3 bakes the gully's p0, p1 and h1 offline in Blender and compresses them in the editor (EditorUtility.CompressTexture, bc7e). This is a named exception to pages baking in the player. It ends at step 5, when the bake and a GPU encoder run in the player and match the golden page hashes.

shellBake.how: A cell's shell atlas is drawn from its things' L2 meshes and their pages, with the shaders in their bake mode, into the shell's own UV1 layout. The cell's pages are built for the bake when they are not resident, and let go after.
shellBake.why: One look source, so a thing reads the same across the L2 to L3 switch; every kind gets its far atlas from its near function, with no far painter per kind.
shellBake.cache: Cells cache their atlases in the disk cache, keyed by the bake hash, and drop one when the change query names a thing in the cell. Never shipped beyond the heart's start date.
shellBake.status: FIRM as the input (decided at step 1); the cost per cell against the city pan's 90 cells a second is unknown, learned before step 5 with the place bake's cost
